# Kconfig - common architecture-specific options

#

menu "Architecture-specific settings"

source "arch/$(ARCH)/Kconfig"

config FPU
	bool "Floating point services"
	default n
	depends on CPU_HAS_FPU
	help
	  This option enables the kernel's floating point services.
	  It is an overarching option that enables the other floating
	  point options below.

config FPU_SHARING
	bool "Floating point sharing"
	depends on FPU && (USERSPACE || !X86)
	help
	  This option enables the lazy context switch of floating point
	  registers. When this option is enabled, the floating point
	  registers are saved and restored only when the thread is using
	  them. This option should be enabled when multiple threads are
	  using floating point registers.

config LAZY_FP_SHARING
	bool "Lazy floating point sharing"
	depends on FPU_SHARING
	select FPU_SHARING
	help
	  This option enables the lazy context switch of floating point
	  registers. When this option is enabled, the floating point
	  registers are saved and restored only when the thread is using
	  them. This option should be enabled when multiple threads are
	  using floating point registers.

config STACK_POINTER_RANDOMIZATION
	bool "Stack pointer randomization"
	depends on !USERSPACE
	help
	  This option enables stack pointer randomization. Every time a
	  thread is scheduled, the stack pointer is moved to a random
	  offset within the thread's stack. This is a security feature
	  that makes it harder to exploit vulnerabilities related to
	  stack corruption.

config THREAD_CUSTOM_DATA
	bool "Thread custom data"
	help
	  This option enables the thread custom data feature. When this
	  option is enabled, an application can store and retrieve a
	  32-bit value in the thread object.

config THREAD_NAME
	bool "Thread names"
	help
	  This option enables the thread name feature. When this option
	  is enabled, an application can assign a name to a thread.
	  This is useful for debugging.

config THREAD_NAME_LEN
	int
	prompt "Maximum thread name length"
	default 32
	range 0 128
	depends on THREAD_NAME
	help
	  This option specifies the maximum number of characters in a thread
	  name. The value must include the null terminator.

config MAX_THREAD_BYTES
	int "Maximum bytes for thread name"
	depends on USERSPACE
	range 3 64
	default 3 if USERSPACE
	help
	  Maximum number of bytes to reserve for a thread's name.
	  Longer names will be truncated. The kernel will still
	  append a NUL terminator. A value of 3 is the minimum to
	  store at least 2 characters plus the NUL.

config ATOMIC_OPERATIONS_BUILTIN
	bool "Use built-in atomic operations"
	help
	  This option enables the use of the toolchain's built-in functions
	  for atomic operations. If this is not enabled, the architecture
	  must provide an implementation of these operations.

config HW_STACK_PROTECTION
	bool "Hardware-based stack protection"
	depends on CPU_HAS_HW_STACK_PROTECTION
	help
	  This option enables hardware-based stack protection. This is a
	  security feature that helps detect stack overflows.

config KERNEL_STACK_RESERVED_BYTES
	int "Reserved kernel stack bytes"
	default 0
	help
	  Number of bytes to reserve at the bottom of the kernel stack.
	  This is useful for architectures that need to store some data
	  at the bottom of the stack.

config BOOT_BANNER
	bool "Display boot banner"
	default y
	help
	  This option enables the display of a banner at boot time.

endmenu

''. Check these unsatisfied dependencies: USERSPACE (=n). See

MAX_THREAD_BYTES in the menuconfig/guiconfig interface. The Application Development Primer, Setting
Configuration Values, and Kconfig - Tips and Best Practices sections of the manual might be helpful
too.
